en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Names of All Tathāgatas,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at the Great Bodhi Enlightenment Site in the Dharma Wilds of the kingdom of Magadha,
having newly attained perfect enlightenment.
He was accompanied by an assembly of eighty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, eighty-four thousand great Brahmā deva-sons were also at the site of enlightenment,
all surrounding and gazing up at the World-Honored One.
At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara.
He rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
Then he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, there is a dhāraṇī of the names of all Tathāgatas.
That dhāraṇī of the names of all Tathāgatas..."
These have been taught by the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in the Bhadrakalpa, the Bhadrakalpa, and the Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitakalpa; now, I too shall speak them,
sustained by the Buddha's majestic power.
Furthermore, for the sake of the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings, I desire to proclaim it.
I pray only that the World-Honored One will look upon me with compassion and grant his protection.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Avalokiteśvara!
You have been able to give rise to the mind of great compassion for the benefit of all sentient beings;
you have explained it according to their needs.
Then, having received the Buddha’s permission, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One,
if there is a person who wishes to recite that dhāraṇī..."
First, one should with utmost sincerity recite the names of the Buddhas,
the Tathāgatas, namely: the Tathāgata Ratnasiṃhavikrāmin, the Tathāgata Ratnamegha,
the Tathāgata Ratnavyūhagarbha, and the Tathāgata Siṃhamahāmegha.
Cloud Lion Tathāgata, Sumeru Tathāgata,
Lion’s Roar Tathāgata, Lion’s Benefit Tathāgata,
Brahma-Sound Tathāgata, and Virtuous Love Tathāgata.
Tathāgata Padmottara and Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara;
Tathāgata Padmasambhava and Tathāgata Sunetra;
Tathāgata Puṣpadhara and Tathāgata Ratnadhara.
Dharmasambhava Tathāgata, Sūryaprabha Tathāgata,
Sūryaprabha Tathāgata, Candraprabha Tathāgata, Amitakośa Tathāgata, and Amitavyūhakośa Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata Amitābha, the Tathāgata Padmagarbha,
the Tathāgata Divyaghoṣa, the Tathāgata Kukūlaparivartana,
and the names of all such Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
If a person hears this and proclaims it to others,
that person will not hear the name of the evil realms for sixty thousand kalpas,
let alone fall into the Avīci Hell.
Then, having spoken these names of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tadyathā | caṭu raścite yojanaśatasahasrāṇi | jātāparāntakūṭaṃ kṛtaṃ | dhāraṇī svāhā ||
1. Hā; 2. Sarva-tathāgata-mūrdhita-dhāraṇī svāhā; 3. Aparājite śaraye svāhā; 4. Sarva-tathāgatoṣṇīṣa... [svāhā].
saṃhara dhāraṇi svāhā | sarvatathāgataprasāda-dharma-saṃbhava-dhāraṇi svāhā | sarvatathāgata...
13. *tāpasi-tā* 14. *saptadhāraṇi svāhā* 15. *padmāpanīkaya svāhā* 16. *aṣṭamahābala-dhāraṇi svāhā* 17. *śrīḥ*
Tavaraṇāya svāhā. (17) Sarvatathāgatānām adhāraṇī svāhā. (18) Āśrite padmaśekhare tathāgatadhāraṇi. (19)
Niṣaha hūṃ (19) padmahasitāya svāhā (20) sarvamantradharāṇyai svāhā (21). At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having spoken this dhāraṇī,
he again addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
this is the dhāraṇī of the names of all Tathāgatas."
If there are good men or good women who receive,
uphold, read, recite, contemplate, remember,
and explain it to others.
All five acts of immediate retribution committed by this person shall be completely eliminated;
after the end of their life, they will be reborn in heaven as a king,
with a lifespan of eighty-four hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas.
Thereafter, he shall attain the rank of a Wheel-Turning King with a lifespan of sixty intermediate kalpas.
Once these kalpas have passed, he shall attain Buddhahood,
named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmagarbha.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
there were eighty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and eighty-four thousand great Brahmā deva-sons.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, and they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Names of All Tathāgatas*, spoken by the Buddha.
